Cluster spectra

Source: R/cluster_spectra.R
cluster_spectra.Rd

Cluster peaks by spectral similarity.

Usage

cluster_spectra(
  peak_table,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_size = 5,
  max_size = NULL,
  nboot = 1000,
  plot_dend = TRUE,
  plot_spectra = TRUE,
  verbose = getOption("verbose"),
  outfile = NULL,
  save = NULL,
  parallel = TRUE,
  max.only = FALSE,
  output = c("pvclust", "clusters"),
  col = palette.colors(palette = "Okabe-Ito")[-c(1, 5, 9)],
  ...
)

Arguments

peak_table

A peak_table object from get_peaktable.

alpha

Significance threshold used to select clusters based on approximately unbiased (AU) bootstrap p-values from pvclust.

min_size

Clusters must contain more than min_size peaks. Defaults to 5.

max_size

Clusters must contain fewer than max_size peaks. Defaults to the number of peaks in peak_table.

nboot

Number of bootstrap replicates for pvclust.

plot_dend

Logical. If TRUE, plots dendrogram with bootstrap values.

plot_spectra

Logical. If TRUE, plots overlapping spectra for each cluster.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints progress report to console.

outfile

Optional path to an .RDS file. If not NULL, the pvclust object is saved to file using saveRDS(). Existing files are overwritten.

save

The save argument is deprecated. Please use outfile instead.

parallel

Logical. If TRUE, use parallel processing for pvclust.

max.only

Logical. If TRUE, returns only highest level cluster from each nested set of clusters. Named to match the argument of the same name in pvrect and pvpick; passed to pvpick.

output

What to return: "pvclust" for the pvclust object, "clusters" for the list of clusters, or both (the default).

col

Colors for each cluster's box and number on the dendrogram and the title of its spectra panel, recycled if there are more clusters than colors. Defaults to the Okabe-Ito palette, without black, yellow and grey.

...

Additional arguments to pvclust.

Value

Returns a named list with an element for each value of output: pvclust, the pvclust object, and clusters, a list of S4 cluster objects.

The cluster objects consist of the following components:

  • peaks: a character vector containing the names of all peaks contained in the given cluster.

  • pval: a numeric scalar containing one minus the approximately unbiased (AU) value that pvclust reports for the given cluster, so that small values indicate strong support.

Details

Before using this function, reference spectra must be attached to the peak_table using the attach_ref_spectra function. These spectra are then used to construct a distance matrix from pairwise Pearson correlations among peaks, and pvclust clusters the peaks hierarchically, with bootstrap resampling. Clusters whose bootstrap support exceeds the confidence set by alpha are returned. Peaks whose reference spectrum is constant are dropped before clustering.

Clusters can be filtered by size using the min_size and max_size arguments. The clustering algorithm often returns nested clusters, so an individual peak can appear in more than one. If max.only is TRUE, only the largest cluster in a nested tree of clusters meeting the confidence threshold is returned.

The example uses nboot = 100 to reduce run time. For real data, the pvclust authors recommend the default of 1000 replicates for a first look, then 10,000 for smaller errors.

References

R. Suzuki & H. Shimodaira. 2006. Pvclust: an R package for assessing the uncertainty in hierarchical clustering. Bioinformatics, 22(12):1540-1542. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btl117 .

Author

Ethan Bass

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("pvclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
data(pk_tab)
data(Sa_warp)
pk_tab <- attach_ref_spectra(pk_tab, Sa_warp, ref = "max.int")
cl <- cluster_spectra(pk_tab, nboot = 100, max.only = FALSE, alpha = 0.03)
}




# }
